claims.claim: The query is a 1-cyclopropyl-6-fluoro-8-methoxy-3-carboxylic acid fluoroquinolone; close fluoroquinolone analogs have measured human absolute oral bioavailability of 87.6–100% (trovafloxacin, levofloxacin, ofloxacin) and antofloxacin shows an oral/IV AUC ratio of about 1.1, providing direct threshold-relevant support for F ≥ 20%.

L6 moxifloxacin records (same 8-methoxy/1-cyclopropyl core) show low human hepatocyte intrinsic clearance (1.56 µL/min/10^6 cells; 3.01 in mouse), indicating low hepatic first-pass; population PK intrinsic CL values (34.4–69.1 L/h) are model-derived and not direct F measurements.

Other L6 records show HLM intrinsic clearance values of 16.09 µL/min/mg (enrofloxacin, described as moderate), 33.49 µL/min/mg (M02), rank-order HLM data for sitafloxacin, and species-specific sulfate clearance in rats, but none provides affirmative threshold-relevant evidence for F < 20%; direct human F records for the class remain high.
No L6 record overturns the direct F evidence; the uncertain physicochemical prior (fully ionized, logD -0.47) is not endpoint proof and does not support a low prediction.
